note: Recorded by verify.py --update-floor, except the *_max ceilings, which are edited BY HAND and never re-measured. `collected` catches tests that stopped being collected; `passed` is compared against passed+skipped, so a check may move between passing and consciously-skipped but the two together may never shrink. The *_max ceilings bound the skipped side: 24/7/2 is exactly what a machine with none of this instance's local prerequisites skips (a GitHub runner: no agent CLIs, no ~/.codex/skills, no /Applications/ChatGPT.app, no populated capability ledger), measured 2026-08-21. On the owner's machine all prerequisites exist and nothing skips at all. Raising a ceiling is a deliberate act: it means agreeing that one more thing is allowed to go unchecked, so say which and why in the commit. RAISED 24 -> 26 on 2026-08-22 for exactly two tests: test_capability_admission.test_safety_guard_exemption_is_declared_and_narrow and test_compute_only_category_must_name_a_control_that_exists. Both assert on DECLARATION-owned ledger fields (kill_switch_category, control_point) that are applied to a running instance and never shipped in the tree, so on a machine with no populated ledger they skip via env_prereq.ledger_declaration_absent rather than fail. That is two more things allowed to go unchecked on a bare runner, and the reason is that the alternative -- asserting machine state as a code expectation -- is what made three other tests red on a correct tree.
